notes.2: The ability to follow a simple key, though often not especially demanding, is never-the-less an important ability at this level. It was reassuring to see so many successfully doing so.
notes.8: This question tested candidates’ knowledge that it is the solvent only that moves by osmosis. The reference here was to the movement of the solute – the red dye. Even so, many believed that the dye would be moving by osmosis rather than by simple diffusion.
notes.9: Many candidates knew that glycerol is a basic unit of oils. It may be that the term ‘oils’ rather than ’fats’ was a source of confusion for some.
notes.10: This proved to be one of the more challenging questions on the paper, with some candidates failing to appreciate the significant difference in the appearance of graphs that show the effect of increased temperature and increased pH on enzymes and their activity.
notes.16: It was expected that candidates would appreciate that a diet lacking in meat would contain plant material which is a source of dietary fibre. This was not well known to all.
notes.17: As with Question 10, the interpretation of graphs proved challenging. Apart from the relatively unlikely option, C, the alternatives proved almost equally popular. Many candidates chose graphs that indicated an increase in humidity will increase the rate of transpiration.
notes.21: This question proved challenging for some and many appeared unsure of the differences in the composition of inspire and expired air.
notes.27: Candidates were required to identify the neurone as motor, and then know that its cell body would lie in the central nervous system. A significant proportion of candidates erroneously indicated that the cell body would be in the leg.
notes.29: The link between alcohol consumption and liver damage was well known by almost all candidates.
notes.32: Many candidates seemed unfamiliar with the different forms of contraception.
notes.38: The concept of food chains is well understood by candidates.
notes.general_comments: The questions on this paper proved challenging to some candidates. The interpretation of graphs is an area where some candidates need further practice.
